answer: An agent economy can plant decoy identities, lures no real user would ever touch, such as an account offering a violet-gated reward or an ivory-signed contract that only a scammer bites. Sybil farms cannot tell these jade-tagged traps from genuine peers, so mass-created clones inevitably interact with them. The network flags any account sharing the decoy interaction graph and slashes its deposit, making large fake-identity campaigns self-expose at near-zero cost to honest agents.
